Special Vehicles – Part 3

🚊 Trams

Tram drivers have a number of special rights in traffic:

✅ Tram Has Priority
  • Always takes precedence over other road users at an equivalent intersection
  • Takes precedence over other road users when turning
⚠ Tram Must Still Give Way To
  • Pedestrians at a pedestrian crossing
  • Crossing drivers on a priority road
  • All applicable traffic signs and road signs

🚎 Trolleybuses (Electric Buses)

A trolleybus is a public bus electrically powered by cables above the road. It does not run on rails — it runs on the road like a regular bus. It is therefore not subject to tram rules.

🚊
Tram
  • Runs on rails
  • Priority at equivalent intersections
  • Priority when turning
  • Subject to tram-specific rules
🚎
Trolleybus
  • Runs on road (no rails)
  • Powered by overhead cables
  • Follows public bus rules
  • Give way when it signals to leave a bus stop in a built-up area

🚛 LZVs and Special Transport

In addition to normal lorries, there are larger vehicles called LZV (Lang Zwaar Voertuig — Long Heavy Vehicle). They are mainly intended for motorway transport.

Normal Lorry
16.5 – 18.75 m
Max length
50 t
Max weight (50,000 kg)
LZV (Long Heavy Vehicle)
max 25.25 m
Max length
60 t
Max weight (60,000 kg)
⚠ Overtaking an LZV

LZVs carry a warning sign on the back: "LET OP! EXTRA LANG." (Attention! Extra long.) Due to the extra length, any overtaking manoeuvre takes significantly longer. Make sure you have enough room before attempting to overtake.

🚨
Convoi Exceptionnel / Exceptional Transport

If something extra large or extra heavy needs to be transported, permission must be requested in advance. These are called convoi exceptionnel, exceptional transport, or uitzonderlijk vervoer (Dutch). They are usually accompanied by escort vehicles with orange flashing lights.

ℹ How to Behave Around Exceptional Transport

Take these transports into account. Do not overtake if there is not enough room, and always keep your distance.
